data.description: It is a temple located at the feet of Margalla Hills in Islamabad. The complex is comprised of two temples and Dharamshala. The complex has been constructed in standard size bricks. Main temple, located on western half is square in plan and superimposed with a bulbous dome erected on an octagonal and circular drum with a finial on the top. The sanctum of the temple on the north, south and western side is divided into three rows of sunken panels on the outer surface.

data.description: The temple is rectangular in plan, measuring 2.8m x 2.8m and its height is 6m. The sanctum is approached by five steps which consists of three pointed arches. The temple is built in standard size burnt bricks and is plastered in lime surkhi. Sanctum is surmounted by a shikara in the shape of inverted lotus while the pinnacle is decorated with lotus motifs. The temple has been white washed now.

data.description: In the north of the Pharwala mosque, there are graves of the Ghakkhar Sultan Adam Khan, Sultan Momare Khan and the tomb of the last ruler Sultan Muqarab Khan. The tomb of Sultan Muqarab Khan is measuring 7x7x3.5m, octagonal in shape, having its entrance to the east. It has low height dome decorated with leaf patterns. In the interior of the tomb, there are three false arches on the remaining three sides, leaving the wall having entrance. The tomb was constructed in stone masonry and plastered with cement in later times.

data.description: The temple is square in plan, built in burnt bricks masonry. The sanctum is surmounted by Shikara. The blind arches decorate its lower portion, while Shikara is ornated with miniature Shikaras. The temple is provided with Garbhagriha having three cusped archways with trefoil design. data.description: The fort of Pharwala (Par Wala) was constructed during the year 1008-1015 CE by Sultan Kai Gohar (the founder of Gakhar Dynasty) in the Sub-continent. The fort has six gateways namely Hathi Gate, Fort Gate, Lashkari Gate, Ziarat Gate, Bagh Gate and Begum Gate. The area of the fort is about 54 sq.km. In history, the fort has been used as Military fort, it had 100 Elephants, 5000 Horses and 10,000 Men stationed inside it. The structure of the fort, mainly the two gateways, parts of the fortification, a mosque and a tomb located on the other bank of Soan River, are in a bad state of preservation. The structures are mainly built-in stone in lime surkhi or mud mortar and are stylistically similar to those of the fort at Rawat. None of the original residential or other buildings survived within the fortification.

data.description: A Sarai, square in plan with two arched gateways provided in the northern and southern walls of the complex. The mosque, built in the north-western corner of the Sarai is completely repaired and plastered with cement mortar. The interior of the mosque is painted with fresco paintings, the remains of the baoli of Suri period, now covered by a mosque of this Sarai has also been reported.

data.description: The Baradari is octagonal in plan, measuring 3.20m high with its circumference measuring 16m. The entrance is 2.20m high and 1m wide. Height of the platform is 2m and thickness of wall is 60cm. Brick measures 16cmx4cm. Main structures are approached by eleven steps. It has been built on a high platform in burnt bricks masonry with lime mortar. The Baradari has four entrances built in multi cusped arches and four false arches. The building of the Baradari has been plastered with lime mortar internally and externally, on which traces of fresco paintings, floral and geometrical designs in red, yellow and green colours are reported.

data.description: A mosque measuring 10m x 5m with surviving height of 5m located close to Pharwala fort. It is rectangular in plan with three entrances provided through rectangular doors in its eastern wall. The mosque has been constructed in limestone with lime mortar plaster from inside. The facade and the interior have recessed decorative panels with pointed arches in small sized burnt bricks. There were three mihrabs in each portion of the mosque in which the central one was for daily prayers while the other two seems to have been carved out for symmetrical purposes and decoration. Rounded domes have been constructed in burnt bricks on the main prayer chamber.

data.description: Rawat, a corruption of an Arabic word Rebat meaning Sarai seems originally to be an ancient Sarai situated about 18 km from Rawalpindi towards Jhelum close to the G.T. Road. The present small fortress-Sarai appears to have been built during the Sultanate period in early 15th Century CE. The fort in its present condition contains two gateways on north and east, a three domes mosque in the middle of the western wing, an octagonal single dome mausoleum on the north-western corner, partly obstructing the frontage of the mosque and numerous scattered graves inside. There are regular rows of identical living cells along the four sides of the quadrangular inner face of the defense walls overlooking the inner courtyard.

data.description: The memorial is constructed on a low recessed platform of three terraces. Lower measures 2.83x2.83m square, second one measures 2.42x2.42m square and the last one measures 1.50m square. Terraces are constructed with single row of sand stone, 12cm thickness. Memorial obelisk is in tapering shape measuring 1.5x1.5m square at the base. Obelisk is 2.20m high, above is stepped parapet. On north-west side of the obelisk is a 76x46cm recessed panel which once had plaque with some inscription, which had been removed, inside of the panel is filled with standard size bricks laid in lime mortar. The height of obelisk is 2.54 m. It is of mid-19th Century CE and has similar architectural traces as Nicolson Monument Taxila. The obelisk is constructed on a cultural mound of Kushan Period; most part of the mound has been levelled by cultivators.

data.description: Golrha Sharif Railway Station was established by the British in 1882 to connect the area to Havelian, Kohat and Peshawar. The building is constructed with lime stone masonry laid out in lime mortar. The small stone platform is designed in Victoria Style railway station. A museum was established in this building which housed rare items, i.e., watches, navigation equipment, medals, costumes worn by railway staff of British India, photographs, crockery, furniture and other railway accessories.

data.name_of_site: Shrine of Meher Ali Shah (Golra Sharif)
data.description: The shrine of Meher Ali Shah - an early 20th-century Sufi scholar of the Chishti order, who was also a leader of the anti-Ahmadiya movement. The shrine is located within the Islamabad Capital Territory, in the village of Golra Sharif. Peer Mehr Ali Shah died on 11 May 1937, and was succeeded by Babuji. The construction of the mausoleum took nearly twenty years to be fully completed. For this purpose, Marble was brought from the Makrana mines in Jodhpur State.
data.title: Mehre Muneer
data.published_in: Biography of Mehre Ali Shah (English Translation)

data.description: The shrine of Hazrat Bari Imam was originally built on the order of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. The shrine of Bari Imam is built on top of Medieval sites; therefore, it is at least 450 years old. Shah Abdul Latif Qadri Qazmi Mashhaddi R.A (Bari Imam) is a well renowned Sufi Saint of the Pothohar region. He is a Wali Allah and spiritual guide of Silsila-e-Qadria, a tariqa, which claimed spiritual supremacy over all other Sufi orders of Hazrat Syed Abdul Qadir Jillani (R.A).
data.title: Shrine of Hazrat Bari Imam (R.A): Study of Shrine in Cultural Context
data.published_in: European Academic Research Vol. II, Issue 8, November 2014

Central dome has been erected on a high drum. Zone of transition has been created with squinches. It is reconstructed by CDA and all the surface decoration has been concealed under the thick paint.

data.description: Shah Allah Ditta Caves are situated on the southern side of Margalla hills in a small picturesque valley, only 14 km north-west of the capital Islamabad, measuring 40m in length, 60m in width and 08m in height. The caves consist of two natural kanjur rock shelters situated on either side of the natural spring. Front side of the eastern cave no.1 is covered with a wall of undressed stone laid in lime mortar. A narrow approach to the cave is provided in the eastern north. Facade of the cave is covered with mud plaster having coatings of red color. Cave no.2 also consists in natural kanjur rock stone. Inside the cave, a small platform (1m in length) is provided. The colour of walls and roof has become blackish due to smoke of the fire used by the inhabitants. In front of the caves, there are remains of a paved channel and a square water tank measuring 9x6 m constructed in lime stone blocks, laid in lime mortar.
